data.title: World-model v0 (WHAM-style)
data.phase: spec landed · blocked on tokenizer round-trip
data.summary: ~500M decoder-only Llama-class AR transformer over interleaved token streams; 125M → 500M curriculum; HF transformers + accelerate FSDP.

sections.body: Llama-class decoder-only, ~500M parameters at the headline size. 28 layers, d_model=1280, 20 attention heads, RoPE, SwiGLU. We use the HuggingFace LlamaForCausalLM with custom embedding init (block-aware) and the WHAM block-weighted CE loss. Speculative or parallel decoding is a v1 question.

One long interleaved sequence per training sample. Per-timestep schema: 
[t] [magnetics block] [low-freq signal block] [visible frame patch* k] [IR frame patch* m] [equil cross-attn key] [scalar actions]
Block boundaries are recorded in BLOCKWEIGHTS so the loader can apply weighted CE.

Optimizer AdamW(0.95, 0.95, 1e-8), weight decay 0.1, cosine LR 6e-4 → 6e-5 over 30k steps. Warmup 500. FSDP across 4 H200; batch size 32 sequences of 16k tokens. Eval every 5k steps on a held-out 1% slice.

Headline demo per demo.html. Training-time hooks: token perplexity per block, magnetics Pearson r on next-step prediction, visible frame rFID on next-frame prediction. All three must be improving by step 10k to continue.

model-size-curriculum.rationale: Validate full pipeline (tokenizer → loader → FSDP training loop) cheaply before committing the full 500M GPU-budget. De-risks FSDP wiring and token-stream bugs; any training-loop issue discovered at 125M costs ~4h exclusive window vs a full 500M run.

notes.body: Architecturally we're a thin layer over HF LlamaForCausalLM; the interesting bits are the block-aware embedding init and the weighted CE loss.

research.title: WHAM — World and Human Action Models

questions.body: Should we use HuggingFace's accelerate FSDP wrapper or roll our own with torch.distributed.fsdp? The wrapper is simpler but pins us to the HF training loop semantics.
